reconcile.note: Clarke reconciles the discovery scenes by placing one brother's money in the mouth of his sack, found en route, and the rest deeper, found only at home.

discrepancy.emptyNote: John Skinner catalogues this as a contradiction, but the project's public-domain source survey found no verbatim critic passage that engages it.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: John Skinner, A Critical and Exegetical Commentary on Genesis (ICC) (1910).

sides.snippet: As one of them opened his sack to give his donkey food in the lodging-place, he saw his money. Behold, it was in the mouth of his sack.
sides.verseText: As one of them opened his sack to give his donkey food in the lodging-place, he saw his money. Behold, it was in the mouth of his sack.

sides.snippet: every man's bundle of money was in his sack
sides.verseText: It happened as they emptied their sacks, that behold, every man's bundle of money was in his sack. When they and their father saw their bundles of money, they were afraid.
